scope: Application-controlled browser networking for full and lean Pages builds; backend/node-only/unshipped research transports are not represented as shipped behavior.
evidenceKind: Source-reviewed inventory with referenced regression suites. Final combined-head browser, security and CI outcomes are recorded separately; static catalog coverage is not proof of all runtime traffic or whole-feature completion.
applicationEnforceable: Reject redirects and unapproved endpoint switching
Omit application cookies/referrer and prevent response caching where APIs permit
Apply selected policy at each app-controlled dispatch and retry
Minimize payloads and avoid keys/secret identifiers in network data
Keep network-free workers behind constrained main-thread bridges
Use same-origin active assets and detect new egress in tests
unavoidableOrExternal: Browser-selected DNS, source IP, TLS/SNI, timing, HTTP Origin/CORS, browser/extension traffic and endpoint logging cannot be fully hidden or governed by a static application.
Public-chain payer, amount, asset, timing and transaction relationships remain visible.
A selected RPC, relayer, oracle or merchant can observe requests it receives.
Host compromise can change JavaScript; an in-app hash is not independent source attestation.
Already-dispatched requests and broadcasts cannot be made unsent by a later policy change or page reload.

policyScopeStatement: Production Services requires an in-memory action capability for application-controlled fetch/RPC. Capabilities bind the selected endpoint, action, network, session and settings revision, and enforce privacy policy on dispatch and response reads. Listed browser-loader, navigation and wallet-provider boundaries are external to this fetch policy. Final combined-head acceptance and independent review are pending; static inventory alone is not proof of runtime isolation.

nonShippedAdapters.change: Honor Request method and cancellation before dispatch; cancellation after dispatch cannot retract bytes.

authorityModel.ordinaryFetch: Default Services.fetchFn rejects unscoped requests; configured endpoint presence alone grants no authority.
authorityModel.lifetime: Grants are in memory only, become stale on session/app-lock/relevant-settings changes, and are never restored after reload. Each dispatch and body read rechecks the grant; active streams are cancelled on invalidation.
authorityModel.crossTab: Storage events for settings, scan privacy, scan lanes and network profiles invalidate grants. Only non-secret preferences are synchronized, not keys or wallet identities. Current stored values are also checked at dispatch and read time.
authorityModel.ownNode: RPC/indexer grants require loopback or valid v3 onion endpoints in own-node mode; approved one-action direct exceptions cannot override own-node. Exact URL or explicit same-origin path-prefix binding prevents changing providers.
authorityModel.exceptions: Only documented Sweep and merchant-profile actions can request one-action direct-path exceptions. They do not authorize other actions or override own-node RPC/indexer constraints.
authorityModel.limits: Authority defaults: 30-second per-dispatch deadline including body; 16 MiB body cap; 10-minute idle grant lifetime. More restrictive adapter limits still apply. Checks reject results queued after browser sleep or a backwards clock change.
limitations: Already-transmitted requests and broadcasts cannot be withdrawn.
Ambient Tor transport, DNS, IP, TLS/SNI, browser extensions and endpoint logs are outside application enforcement.
Source-level grants do not by themselves prove the UI obtained the intended action consent; browser and independent review must check the call sites.
